extracted.intended_audience: practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO (patent attorneys/agents), OED staff, and other stakeholders in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO disciplinary standards and sanctions applicable to registered patent practitioners, including the governing rules of professional conduct, example misconduct, probation conditions, reporting requirements, and the procedural steps for addressing noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring practitioners to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: not timely preparing and filing a provisional application for Client #1; not timely responding to the Notice to File Corrected Application Papers (Notice of Correction) in Client #2's application. Such failures are cited as violations of § 11.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring practitioners to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: failing to respond to Client #1's inquiries regarding the status of the provisional application; failing to respond to Client #2's status requests; failing to inform Client #2 about the USPTO Notice of Correction or the subsequent Notice of Abandonment. These communication failures are cited as violations of § 11.104(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered practitioners subject to USPTO jurisdiction and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 et seq.) and to disciplinary jurisdiction under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office has statutory and regulatory authority to investigate, impose discipline, and approve settlement agreements for registered patent practitioners. Maintaining registration and compliance with USPTO rules is a continuing obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct constituting violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factual examples that constitute violations of the rules: failing to file a client's provisional application in a timely manner; failing to inform clients about the status of filings; failing to respond to USPTO notices that warn 'to avoid abandonment;' allowing a client's application to go abandoned without informing the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete acts and omissions (detailed in the Stipulated Facts) are illustrative of conduct that will be treated as breaches of the duties of diligence and client communication under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and imposed — public reprimand and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary sanctions can include public reprimand and a probationary period; in this case Respondent is publicly reprimanded and placed on an eighteen (18) month probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets probation length (18 months) and specific conditions the practitioner must satisfy during probation; public reprimand will be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation reporting requirements — mental health and performance letters
rubrics_metrics.description: During the probationary period the practitioner must, every six months, provide the OED Director with letters from: (i) his mental health professional confirming there is no mental health reason precluding the practitioner from performing patent-related employment duties; and (ii) a registered patent attorney confirming the practitioner is performing his patent-related employment duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are due every six months starting on the date the Final Order is signed. These are affirmative, recurring evidentiary conditions of probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation condition — notify OED of employer changes
rubrics_metrics.description: During the probationary period, the practitioner shall inform the OED Director whenever he changes his employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ongoing reporting obligation during probation to ensure OED oversight of the practitioner's employment circumstances relevant to compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for addressing alleged probation noncompliance (Order to Show Cause and suspension request)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED is of the good faith opinion that the practitioner failed to comply with the Agreement, Final Order, or USPTO Rules during probation, OED shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the practitioner's last address of record, and grant thirty days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after considering any response OED continues to believe there was noncompliance, OED will deliver the Order to Show Cause, the practitioner's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request the Director enter an order immediately suspending the practitioner for up to thirty (30) days for the violations set forth in the Legal Conclusions. If suspended and the practitioner seeks review, the review will not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Official Gazette notice summarizes the practitioner's registration number, the nature of the sanction (public reprimand and probation length), the conduct (failure to timely communicate and allowing abandonment), the specific Rules violated (§ 11.103 and § 11.104(a)(3)), and notes the settlement basis and mitigating considerations. Publication is a required consequence of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, in future matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct; and (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against the practitioner — as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or to rebut any statement or representation by or on the practitioner's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating factors in reaching a settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may give favorable consideration to credible mitigating information when resolving disciplinary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the OED Director favorably considered the practitioner's statement that he was suffering from extreme personal issues (severe depression) at the time of representation, that he sought and continues successful treatment, and that his move to a law firm providing technical support improved docketing and communications. Such factors influenced the settlement and sanction selection.
